slides.copy:
you love the house.
try the drive home.
a valley house-hunting check
slides.visual_direction: Navy statement cover, large staggered headline; a single small route arrow, not a geographic map.

slides.copy:
sunday’s tour is one trip.
your workday is another.
test the trip you’ll actually repeat.
slides.visual_direction: Cream moment layout; emphasis on “workday,” ample space.

slides.copy:
test your usual trip.
on a day and time you’d normally go.
compare routes that fit your destination.
slides.visual_direction: Steel-blue spot layout; two plain route labels, no invented speeds or travel times.

slides.copy:
write down the whole trip.
leaving the house → arriving
parking → walking in
then check the way home.
slides.visual_direction: Navy comparison layout; outward and return rows.

slides.copy:
keep the house on the list.
add the drive beside it.
then decide how the day feels.
slides.visual_direction: Her archive exterior with its illustrative-photo label; no location or price claim.

slides.copy:
save this for the next tour.
the house and the drive belong
in the same decision.
slides.visual_direction: Cream close, handle and disclosure footer.

caption:
you can love a house and still want to try the drive before you get attached.

when you’re looking around the valley, check the trip from the actual street at the time you normally leave. ventura boulevard and the freeway are two routes to compare when both work for your destination. include parking, and check the way back too.

you don’t need a perfect commute. you need a clear picture of the one you’d be choosing.

save this for your next tour.

Jennifer Santulan · Equity Union · DRE #01914509

slides.copy:
buying on your own.
five opinions in your head.
slides.visual_direction: Jen’s real studio portrait, text above/left. Small First Home Valley label.

slides.copy:
someone loves the kitchen.
someone would wait.
you’re the one choosing where to live.
slides.visual_direction: Cream moment; no imaginary message bubbles or testimonial styling.

slides.copy:
put your own question first.
what do i still need to understand
about this home?
slides.visual_direction: Navy statement, handwritten “your question” once.

slides.copy:
then take it to the right person.
loan question → lender
condition question → inspector
search and next steps → me
slides.visual_direction: Steel-blue comparison; large type, no icons competing with words.
Archive living-room detail, illustrative label; text on empty wall.

slides.copy:
your decision can have support.
keep this for the day
everyone has an opinion.
slides.visual_direction: Cream close, simple Jen lockup.

caption:
buying on your own can still come with a lot of opinions.

one person loves the kitchen. someone else thinks you should wait. before you try to settle every opinion, write down the question that is actually yours.

is it about the loan, the condition of the home, or what happens next? that tells us who needs to explain it. i can help with the search and the next steps; the lender and inspector handle their parts.

you get to understand the decision you’re making.

keep this for the day the advice gets loud.

Jennifer Santulan · Equity Union · DRE #01914509

slides.copy:
they needed more time
to find the next home.
from my transaction archive
slides.visual_direction: Jen’s studio portrait; small Listing Launch label. Never a client or property photo from another case.

slides.copy:
the search was taking longer.
and the timing mattered.
slides.visual_direction: Navy moment; no invented calendar dates or countdown.

slides.copy:
i negotiated a longer escrow
with a contingency.
a condition written into the agreement.
slides.visual_direction: Cream statement; no contract replica.

slides.copy:
the terms deserve attention too.
price is one part.
timing is another.
slides.visual_direction: Steel-blue comparison: price / timing, no dollar values.

slides.copy:
that’s one part of my job.
looking at how the move
will actually happen.
slides.visual_direction: Navy statement; no promised payoff or “saved the deal” label.

slides.copy:
buying and selling?
bring the timing question too.
my DMs are open.
slides.visual_direction: Cream close, Jen identity.

caption:
a moment from my transaction archive: the buyers were still looking for their next home, and time was becoming part of the problem.

i negotiated a longer escrow with a contingency—a condition in the agreement. that is the part of this story i want to point out. the work can include the timing of the move, as well as the price of the home.

this was one transaction. different terms need agreement, and the same arrangement won’t fit every move.

buying and selling? bring the timing question too.

slides.copy:
two buyers. one address.
try both trips.
looking together in the valley
slides.visual_direction: Navy cover, two small arrows pointing toward one home symbol. Small First Home Valley label.

slides.copy:
put both trips on the page.
where you need to go.
when you need to arrive.
slides.visual_direction: Cream moment, two equal columns; no gendered icons.

slides.copy:
start from the same street.
check each route at its usual time.
include the trip back.
slides.visual_direction: Steel-blue spot, clearly a blank comparison layout, not a real map.

slides.copy:
add how often you make the trip.
a daily drive and an occasional drive
may matter differently to you.
slides.visual_direction: Navy comparison with “how often?” as the handwritten accent.

slides.copy:
decide what you can each live with.
then compare the houses
against that decision.
slides.visual_direction: Cream statement; no claim that one preference should win.

slides.copy:
stuck between two valley streets?
send me the two options
and what you’re trying to balance.
slides.visual_direction: Navy close, open-DM line and Jen disclosure.

caption:
two people can like the same house and have very different trips home.

before your next valley tour, put both routes beside the same street. check the times you actually travel and how often you make each trip. a longer drive once in a while may feel different from one you make every day.

then talk about what each of you can live with. the house search gets a clearer question to answer.

stuck between two valley streets? send me the two options and what you’re trying to balance. street names or general areas are enough.

Jennifer Santulan · Equity Union · DRE #01914509
